FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Weather, road conditions, traffic volume and time of day can greatly increase the stopping distance you need. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
Keep to posted limits and the pace of traffic; much faster means constant passing, and much slower causes back-ups and unpredictability. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
At a zipper merge where two lanes become one, use both lanes equally until just before the closure, then take turns into the open lane; drivers who wait until the lane ends are doing it right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Slow zones calling for lower speed and extra attention include shopping centers, schools, parks and playgrounds, residential streets, rush hour, narrow bridges, toll plazas and rail crossings. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
Officers make traffic stops on reasonable suspicion of a traffic or criminal violation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
When you see emergency lights or hear a siren behind you, stay calm, signal and pull off or to the right as soon as it is safe; the officer may ask you to move farther from traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
Once stopped, shut off the engine and audio, stay inside unless told otherwise, use interior lights at night, keep hands visible and follow instructions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A01
The officer may come to either side; lower that window, mention any weapon in the vehicle at first contact without reaching for it, and wait for instructions before reaching for documents. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A01
An officer not in uniform will normally show credentials, and you may ask to see them if they do not. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A01
The officer will usually explain the stop and ask for your license, proof of insurance and registration; if those are out of reach, say where they are and wait for an okay before getting them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A01
If asked to step out, keep your hands visible and stand where directed; the officer may give a warning, a ticket that may carry a fine, or make an arrest, and you may ask what action is being taken. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A01
Do not argue at the roadside; contest a decision in court instead, and ask for a supervisor soon after the stop if you think the officer acted improperly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A01
Signing a traffic ticket does not admit guilt, but refusing to sign it can lead to arrest. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A01
Sharing the road means everyone has the right to use it and the duty to obey traffic laws and watch out for one another, keeping in mind that bicycles, motorcycles, buses and trucks handle differently. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A01
Lane filtering lets a two-wheeled motorcycle pass stopped vehicles in its lane when traffic in neighboring lanes is also stopped, there is room, and it goes no faster than 15 miles per hour. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A02
Trucks and buses need more room to turn and change lanes, so stay behind white stop bars at signs and signals, which are often placed to leave trucks turning room. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A02
No Zones are blind areas around trucks and buses where cars vanish from view or sit so close the driver cannot stop or maneuver safely, which greatly raises crash risk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A02
Never pass or stop close behind a truck or bus that is backing or about to back, because the trailer hides objects in its No Zone. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A02
Pass trucks quickly and on the left when you can, and do not cut back in front until both of its headlights show in your rearview mirror, since trucks need longer to slow down. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A02
Do not tailgate a truck or bus: its driver cannot see you behind it, and it blocks your own view of traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A02
Trucks and buses have much larger side blind spots than cars, so a sudden lane change or emergency move by the driver could hit you there. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A02
Trucks and buses often swing into the left lane to turn right, so never squeeze between one and the curb or shoulder. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A02
Runaway truck ramps stop vehicles whose brakes fail; chaining up, changing a tire or parking on a ramp or its entrance is illegal and unsafe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A02
Smoke from the brakes is one sign of a runaway truck or bus, so get out of its way and never get in front of it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A02
Buses stop often, so stay alert behind them, and take care passing a stopped bus because it may pull into your lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A02
A bus pulling out of a drop-off spot into traffic has the right-of-way, and you should watch for riders waiting, getting off or loading bikes in front of it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A02
Take extra care near school buses in neighborhoods and school zones, where students board, leave and cross the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A02
Overhead yellow warning lights mean a school bus is about to stop for children and stay on until the door opens, when the red STOP lights and STOP arm come on. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F29 | anchor: A02
Stay stopped at least 20 feet from the front or rear bumper of a school bus until the driver pulls in the STOP arm and turns off the red lights; failing to stop is illegal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F30 | anchor: A02
When a school bus shows alternating flashing red lights from front or rear, stop at least 20 feet before it and go on carefully only after the lights stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F31 | anchor: A02
On a divided highway of four or more lanes with a median, only traffic behind the school bus must stop; on a two-lane road, or a four-lane road with no median, traffic both ways must stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F32 | anchor: A02
Where a highway has a shared center turn lane and five or more lanes, the duty to stop falls only on the lanes behind the bus, not on oncoming traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F33 | anchor: A02
A light rail vehicle can weigh up to 40 tons and cannot stop quickly, so never turn in front of one and check every direction before turning across light rail tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F34 | anchor: A02
In light rail areas watch for riders boarding and leaving, and stay alert because buildings and plants can hide the trains. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F35 | anchor: A02
Traffic lights, warning lights and gates at light rail crossings all mean stop and do not cross; never drive around a gate, even right after a train passes, since another may come from the other way. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F36 | anchor: A02
Light rail overhead wires hang at a standard 18 feet, 6 inches above the track center; treat any hanging wire as live, never touch it, and report it or faulty safety devices to RTD. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F37 | anchor: A02
Treat a railroad crossbuck like a yield sign, and a sign below it shows how many tracks the crossing has when there is more than one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F38 | anchor: A02
Commercial buses and hazardous-materials trucks must stop at most railroad crossings, so be ready to stop when following one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F39 | anchor: A02
Most motorist-caused crashes with bicycles or motorcycles involve a driver turning left in front of the oncoming rider, so look for riders at the right of the lane or on the shoulder, look again and judge their speed first. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec12-F40 | anchor: A02
Bicycles are vehicles under state law with the same duty to obey rules, signs and markings; at normal traffic speed they may use the full lane, on a multi-lane one-way street they may ride on either side, and you should not honk to startle them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0023]
